description: Case A (invite issued without --public-url, so its endpoint is the issuer's loopback URL). Simulated the recipient's view on one machine by making that loopback address unreachable: Join project shows "Project authority unavailable; retry this attempt / The project's hub is unreachable, so this can't finish yet. Retry when it is back; nothing was lost." Retrying can never succeed from another computer. The catalog-predicted INVALID_INVITATION "Remote invitations require HTTPS" never appears (a hub refuses a non-loopback http --public-url at start: INVALID_ARGUMENT "Public gateway must be an explicit HTTPS origin, or an HTTP origin on loopback").
expected: The recipient is told the invitation points at a computer-local address and must be reissued from a client with a reachable --public-url; the sender is warned at creation (F-036-01).
actual: A generic "retry later" message that leads Marcus and Priya to wait.
suggested_fix: Detect a loopback endpoint on a different client during join and return a distinct code (e.g. INVITATION_UNREACHABLE) with a hint for the sender.
